content:
Reproduction: https://github.com/pandaman64/lean4-module-tests/blob/36549f562d178ca292e457cb0b17644aaae848fa/ModuleTests/Third.lean
Version: v4.28.0, v4.29.0-rc4

I came across a weird unknown namespace error when opening a namespace in a module, when the following conditions satisfy:

  • A module defines public constants in a namespace N.
  • Another module defines additional public constants in the same namespace N
  • The third module, importing the second module, shows the error at open N.

It seems import all Second fixes the issue, but the behavior is unintuitive. Should I open an issue?
Can you please dump the file contents here so that everyone doesn’t have to click 10 buttons to see your actual repro?

Here you are:

ModuleTests/First.lean

module

namespace Hello

-- Repro step 1: A module has a definition in a namespace
public def greet := "hello"

end Hello

ModuleTests/Second.lean

module

-- Repro step 2: Another module imports the first module, and adds a definition to the same namespace.
-- Commenting out the import fixes the error.
import ModuleTests.First

namespace Hello

public def world := "world"

end Hello

ModuleTests/Third.lean

module

import ModuleTests.Second
-- import all ModuleTests.Second -- This fixes the error

-- Repro step 3: Opening the namespace fails
open Hello

-- Even though this module can access public definitions in the namespace
#check Hello.world
